column5: Group recorded mean temperature to 0.1 degC, then convert group temperature to kelvin by adding 273.15. Native C_vol is the arithmetic mean of three specimens. Its separate sample SD uses n-1=2 and is descriptive, not a confidence/calibration uncertainty bound. Extra digits represent arithmetic only. Linear interpolation of means is an authored approximation with no certified interpolation error or extrapolation; scatter remains discrete. No density enters native capacity.

Vinyl_Plank_Flooring_Density_Wet_R1.csv: header Vinyl_Plan_Flooring_WET_1, mass 67.0 g, volume 103.8 cm3, density 645 kg/m3; Vinyl_Plank_Flooring_Density_Wet_R2.csv: header Vinyl_Plan_Flooring_WET_2, mass 67.6 g, volume 100.1 cm3, density 676 kg/m3; Vinyl_Plank_Flooring_Density_Wet_R3.csv: header Vinyl_Plan_Flooring_WET_3, mass 67.4 g, volume 100.6 cm3, density 670 kg/m3. The source reduction averages the reported rounded density columns to 663.66666666666663 kg/m3, rather than recomputing mass/volume ratios. Measurement temperature is unreported. This is a source normalization input, not rho(T), current installed density or an expansion law.

Divide population-mean native capacity and its sample SD by the condition-mean density 663.66666666666663 kg/m3, then round to whole J/(kg K). Means at 10,20,30,40 degC are 1246,1280,1326,1351; reported-reduction SD are 10,10,10,10. No per-specimen density normalization, density-scatter propagation or measured covariance is supplied. Cp, native C_vol and normalization density are algebraically related. Cp interpolation is an authored approximation.

Units W/(m K). The source pools three cycles from each of three specimens by integer mean temperature, then rounds mean and sample SD (n-1=8) to 0.001. Means are 0.07,0.074; SD 0.001,0.001. Nine readings are not nine independent specimens. Plate setpoints 5/25 and 35/55 degC give 20 K upward through-thickness gradients. Source temperature groups are mean test temperatures. Conditioning-specific source populations remain separate, even when rounded k happens to agree.

Thermal-conductivity requires mean-test-temperature-as-local-model=1. It interprets the finite-gradient apparent coefficient as a local through-thickness scalar at numerical mean temperature, with linear interpolation between the two source groups. Apparent-thermal-conductivity retains test-mean-temperature. Neither interpretation resolves unknown filler/layer structure, deconvolves the finite plate gradient or qualifies other material axes or service conditions.
